title: Pilot ladder rigging (2D diagram preview) | maritime insight
description: How to rig a pilot ladder the way the new IMO pilot transfer standards require: 1.5 to 9 metres climb, position clear of discharges and flat on the hull, 48 kN strong points and the gear at the access point. From 1 January 2028 ladders also leave service after 30 months in use or 36 months from manufacture.

source.title: Performance standards for pilot transfer arrangements, resolution MSC.576(110)
New IMO requirements for pilot transfer arrangements
Safety bulletin 02/25: proper maintenance and rigging of pilot transfer arrangements

script: A pilot ladder is life-saving equipment. Rig it wrong, and the person climbing it can fall. Alone, a pilot ladder covers a climb of 1.5 to 9 metres. Above 9 metres, add an accommodation ladder. Hang it clear of discharges, inside the parallel body, every step flat against the hull. The pilot sets the height of the lowest step. Secure it to strong points rated at least 48 kilonewtons, never to the accommodation ladder platform. At the access point: a lifebuoy with self-igniting light, a heaving line, two manropes, and a responsible officer talking to the bridge. From 2028, a ladder leaves service after 30 months in use, or 36 months from manufacture, whichever comes first. Inspect it before and after every use. Rig it as if you were climbing. How to rig a pilot ladder the way the new IMO pilot transfer standards require: 1.5 to 9 metres climb, position clear of discharges and flat on the hull, 48 kN strong points and the gear at the access point. In this video:
• Pilot ladder alone: 1.5 to 9 m
• Clear, inside the parallel body, flat on the hull
• Strong points, not shortcuts
• Ready before the pilot boat arrives
• Ladder withdrawn from service after
• Inspect before and after every use
